people.name: Mama Ireti Adeyemi
people.bio: She kept the family in her head: births, quarrels, and who owed whom a visit.
memories: She sold oranges by the mosque and knew every child on the street by name.

people.name: Baba Ayo Adeyemi
people.bio: A tailor. People still describe cloth by the way he would have cut it.
memories: He kept buttons in a tobacco tin and hummed highlife while he sewed.

people.name: Tunde Adeyemi
people.bio: Moved to Ghana. The family has his name, and not much else.

people.name: Mama Folake Adeyemi
people.bio: She ran the house in Ibadan and did not take corrections on her cooking.
memories: Her jollof was a little sweet, and she would not apologise for it.

people.name: Funke Adeyemi
people.bio: Daughter of Ayo and Folake. She is who the younger ones call when a name is missing.
memories: She still ties her gele the way Folake taught her, even on an ordinary Sunday.

people.name: Kola Balogun
people.bio: Funke's husband. His own parents have not been written down.
memories: He starts laughing before the joke is finished.

people.name: Bisi Adeyemi
people.bio: Funke's sister. She is the one who notices when a name is about to be lost.
memories: She writes names in the back of her bible when a baby is born, so nobody has to argue later.

people.name: Seyi Balogun
people.bio: Keeps this ofrenda, and is still learning which questions to ask.
memories: Seyi started this altar so a story would have somewhere to sit.
